**No, not yet.** Inflation in Australia is above the RBA's 2–3% target and has been rising again for most of the past year.

**Latest figures (ABS monthly CPI, August 2026)**
- **Headline CPI: 4.0%** for the year, up from 3.5% in July. It peaked at 4.6% in March 2026.
- **Trimmed mean: 3.6%.** This is the RBA's preferred measure of underlying inflation. It has been stuck at 3.6% since June 2026 and is the highest it has been in the monthly data shown.

**How it got here**
- **Inflation was nearly under control in mid-2025.** Headline inflation fell to 1.9% in June 2025, and underlying inflation was 2.8%, inside the target band.
- **Then it picked up again.** Headline inflation was back above 3% from July 2025. Underlying inflation has risen steadily, from 3.1% in July 2025 to 3.3% for most of late 2025 and early 2026, then to 3.6% from June 2026.
- **This isn't just one-off price swings.** Because the trimmed mean strips out extreme price moves, its rise suggests price pressure is spreading across many items.

**How the RBA has responded**
- In 2025 the RBA cut the cash rate from 4.35% to 3.60%.
- From February 2026 it reversed course and raised it back to about **4.35% by June 2026**.
- The September 2026 average was 4.36%. That small uptick could mean another rise took effect right at the end of the month, but the monthly averages can't confirm it.

**Bottom line:** Inflation isn't under control. Headline inflation is 4.0% and underlying inflation is 3.6%, both well above the 2.5% midpoint the RBA aims for. Underlying inflation hasn't started falling yet, even after about 0.75 percentage points of rate rises this year. The most hopeful sign is that it seems to have levelled off at 3.6% over the last three months (June to August 2026). We'll need to see it actually fall before we can say inflation is under control.
